summary_paragraph: A woman with ESRD on thrice-weekly hemodialysis via a right femoral tunneled catheter and HIV on antiretroviral therapy presented after noticing the catheter cuff and several centimeters of tubing had migrated out with catheter malfunction, preventing scheduled dialysis. She underwent an uncomplicated over-the-wire exchange of the right femoral tunneled dialysis catheter by Interventional Radiology on the night of admission, with subsequent successful hemodialysis on the day of discharge and no evidence of bloodstream infection (blood cultures with no growth to date). She also reported nontraumatic left great and second toe pain; foot X-ray showed no acute fracture and symptoms were managed with supportive pain control with slight improvement by discharge. She was discharged home with instructions to monitor the catheter site closely and to take all prescribed medications consistently, including HIV therapy and renal-related medications, and to follow up with her primary care clinician and continue scheduled dialysis.
problems: Mechanical complication of other vascular device, implant, and graft (malfunctioning/dislodged femoral hemodialysis catheter)
Other specified procedures as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication (catheter exchange)
End stage renal disease on hemodialysis
Asymptomatic HIV infection status on antiretroviral therapy and opportunistic infection prophylaxis
Myalgia/myositis manifested as left toe pain without fracture
Atrial fibrillation (history of paroxysmal AF; rate/rhythm stable during admission)
Secondary hyperparathyroidism of renal origin (on cinacalcet and phosphate binder)
